messages.subject: secr.fit fails to converve in multi-session analysis despite mask.check yielding LL estimate
parts:
Hello SECR group,

 


 

Hello SECR group,

 

I'm working on a rather large multi-session SECR analysis of small mammal trapping data (10 sessions, 4 occasions, 4600 trap sites, >380 individuals captured >680 times). The study design is a randomized complete block design with 10 blocks and 5 treatments per block, I've specified each block as a different session. The trapping array has approximately the same effort across treatments (96 traps), but the spatial arrangement of the trapping grids within the treatments varies considerably, so I've specified the trapping grid as a list of unique trapping grids for each Session. There are large gaps in the session specific grid so I’m using a mask of type “trapbuffer”. While I have been successful at getting SECR to produce estimates with this design for a previous year's trapping data the model for my 2018 data is not converging. I have tried adjusting the starting values to those similar to other model output but that has not helped convergence.I have tried both the default algorithm and the Nelder-Mead.  I'm not surprised by this lack of convergence given the size of the problem but I'm a bit perplexed as to why mask.check produces a LL estimate for these data but secr.fit cannot. Does make.mask evaluate the influence of buffer size and spacing across all sessions or just the first session? I've noticed mask.check only prints: Session 1 fitting models… to the console nothing about the other sessions. Some output below


Thanks

 

Sean

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: secr.fit fails to converve in multi-session analysis despite mask.check yielding LL estimate
parts:
Hi Sean
It's a real challenge to work with such a large design. 'mask.check' is for one session at a time; it's not telling you anything useful.

You refer to 'nonconvergence', but the real issue seems to be suitable starting values: unless you start out with a viable parameter vector, likelihood maximisation will go nowhere. I suggest you play around some more.

I've also sometimes found that NA log-likelihood with a half-normal detection function is due to a few extreme movements that are wildly unlikely with that short-tailed function. Long movements may be data errors; if real then they may be better handled with a longer-tailed function (exponential).

It may help to start with CL = TRUE to restrict the problem to suitable g0, sigma at first. Maybe there is enough between-session variation that a model homogeneous across sessions is not going to work.

I hope one of these guesses helps.
Murray

Hi Murray,

Thanks for getting back to me. The issue was a few long-distance movements in the data. I neglected to remember to specify tracks=T when plotting the capture histories which would have allowed me to identify them sooner. With those few observations removed I am now getting parameter estimates.

Thanks again.

Sean
